requirements.evidence: 6x full bases: 3 on level 0 (0,0;0,1;1,0) + 3 on level 1 stacked with snaps, capped with 3 top covers. Height 160mm two storeys.
Two notch drawer frames: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) providing full drawers on level 0.
Compact L footprint suitable for workbench; top deck (f22) staged with tape measure and pliers as workshop props, covers provide flat work surface.

finish.summary: Two-storey L-shaped tower (3+3 bases) with two notch drawers on ground level, top covers, end caps and joint bolts. Dressed with workshop props on the top deck.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your storage tower is on the way — I'll get the two-storey frame and drawers sorted.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
